applies_why: The judge text does not count a cited-in verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it instead says the targeted curse limb was dropped, leaving no live link to contradict.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: The phrase 'counts as an unanswered witness' / 'counts toward a broken link': I weighed reading K-G4 as applying to any use of C4 as a live contradiction, against reading it as applying only when the judge counts a cited-in verse as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link; the latter fits the text because the judge treats the limb as dropped.
why: Because the judge does not count C4 as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link, K-G4's quote-and-name requirement is not triggered.
